headline: SCHUMER: HUANG BROKE
dek: The Senate Democratic leader accused Nvidia’s reinstated CEO of shipping advanced chips to China. Administration officials say they’ve seen no evidence of a crime.

items.title: SCHUMER · NOV. 24
items.text: Huang “shipped extremely advanced chips to China, violating US export control law … the equivalent of selling rocket engines to the Soviets during the Space Race.”

items.title: HIS ASK
items.text: Pass the bipartisan export-control bills to “cut off the flow of AI chips and manufacturing equipment to China.”

items.title: VANCE · NOV. 25
items.text: The accusations “were based on anonymous reporting, not on actual evidence.” He said he was told Huang is under no investigation.

items.title: AG BLANCHE
items.text: Concluded there was no evidence Huang broke any laws, based on probes of two Nvidia customers, Reuters reports.

items.title: NVIDIA
items.text: A spokesman said all its shipments were legal and government-authorized (Nov. 19). It didn’t immediately comment on Schumer.

steps.text: Schumer posts the accusation on X
Vance: he’s seen no evidence of a crime
Huang due before House panels and Senate Banking

means.label: Megaspeed probe:
means.text: The Justice and Commerce Departments said Megaspeed, the firm at the center of the case, is under criminal investigation for possible chip smuggling, the NYT reported.

means.label: Both parties:
means.text: GOP Sen. Tom Cotton also says Congress will pass chip export-control bills, including his Chip Security Act.

means.label: Next:
means.text: Lawmakers can question Huang directly next week.

sources: Sources: Sen. Chuck Schumer on X, Nov. 24, 2026; CNBC (Vance remarks), Nov. 25; Reuters via CNBC; The New York Times via The Business Times, Nov. 19; The Guardian, Nov. 24; Reuters via The Independent.
